He played [[college basketball]] for [[Fresno State Bulldogs men's basketball|Fresno State]]. Robinson has played for the [[Miami Heat]], [[Sacramento Kings]], [[Toronto Raptors]] and [[Orlando Magic]] in his NBA tenure. ==High school career== Robinson began his high school career at [[Centennial High School (Las Vegas)|Centennial High School]] in [[Las Vegas]]. Prior to his junior season, he transferred to [[Cathedral High School (Los Angeles)|Cathedral High School]] in [[Los Angeles]] and scored 29 points in his first game.{{cite web|first=Dylan|last=Callaghan-Croley|title=Georgia Tech Basketball Recruiting: Jackets fast rising west coast power forward Orlando Robinson|url=https://yellowjackedup.com/2018/04/24/georgia-tech-basketball-jackets-land-transfer-james-banks-texas/|work=Yellow Jacked Up|publisher=[[FanSided]]|date=April 24, 2018|access-date=July 16, 2021}} Robinson attended Middlebrooks Academy for his senior season. On October 11, 2018, he committed to [[Fresno State Bulldogs men's basketball|Fresno State]] over offers from [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] and [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State]].{{cite news|first=Robert|last=Kuwada|title=Fresno State lands commitment from versatile big man Orlando Robinson|url=https://www.fresnobee.com/sports/college/mountain-west/fresno-state/bulldogs-basketball/article219901350.html|work=[[The Fresno Bee]]|date=October 11, 2018|access-date=July 16, 2021}} ==College career== Robinson averaged 12.2 points and 6.6 rebounds per game as a freshman.{{cite news|first=Jackson|last=Moore|title=Fresno State's Orlando Robinson invited to G League Elite Camp|url=https://247sports.com/college/fresno-state/Article/Fresno-State-basketball-Orlando-Robinson-invited-to-G-League-Elite-Camp-166557732/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=June 14, 2021|access-date=July 17, 2021}} In the offseason, he worked on his ballhandling and strength training in the midst of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite news|first=Robert|last=Kuwada|title=Fresno State's Orlando Robinson has NBA potential. Here's how he's getting training done|url=https://www.fresnobee.com/sports/college/mountain-west/fresno-state/bulldogs-basketball/article242477011.html|work=[[The Fresno Bee]]|date=May 15, 2020|access-date=July 16, 2021}} On January 4, 2021, he scored a career-high 33 points and had 13 rebounds in an 81–61 win against [[Wyoming Cowboys basketball|Wyoming]].{{cite news|title=Robinson scores 33 to carry Fresno St. over Wyoming 81–61|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401262572|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 4, 2021|access-date=July 16, 2021}} As a sophomore, Robinson averaged 14.6 points, 9.2 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game and had 11 double-doubles. He was named to the Second Team All-[[Mountain West]] and received CoSIDA Academic All-District honors. Following the season, Robinson declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite news|first=Julia|last=Lopez|title=Fresno State's Orlando Robinson declares for NBA Draft|url=https://www.yourcentralvalley.com/sports/local-sports/fresno-states-orlando-robinson-declares-for-nba-draft/|work=[[KSEE]]|date=April 29, 2021|access-date=July 16, 2021}} On July 2, 2021, he withdrew from the draft and returned to Fresno State for his junior season.{{cite news|first=Jesús|last=Cano|title=Orlando Robinson will return to Bulldogs for 2021-2022 season|url=https://fscollegian.com/2021/07/orlando-robinson-will-return-to-bulldogs-for-2021-2022-season|work=The Collegian|date=July 2, 2021|access-date=July 16, 2021}} Robinson was named to the First Team All-Mountain West as a junior.{{cite press release|title=Mountain West Reveals 2021-22 Men's Basketball All-Conference Teams|url=https://themw.com/news/2022/3/8/athlete-awards-mountain-west-reveals-2021-22-mens-basketball-all-conference-teams.aspx|website=TheMW.com|publisher=[[Mountain West Conference]]|date=March 8, 2022|access-date=March 8, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Miami Heat / Sioux Falls Skyforce (2022–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Robinson was signed by the [[Miami Heat]] on July 14, 2022.{{cite web|first=Azam|last=Masood|title=Orlando Robinson: Making A Statement|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/orlando-robinson-making-a-statement|website=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2022|access-date=July 21, 2022}} On October 24, 2022, Robinson joined the Heat's [[G League]] affiliate, the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]], for training camp.{{cite web|title=SKYFORCE ANNOUNCES TRAINING CAMP ROSTER AHEAD OF 2022-23 SEASON|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2022-23-season/|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}} On November 13, Robinson was signed to a [[two-way contract]] with the Heat.{{cite web|title=Heat Sign Orlando Robinson to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-orlando-robinson-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=November 13, 2022|access-date=November 14, 2022}} He was waived by the Heat on November 25, and subsequently re-joined the Skyforce.{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN DRU SMITH TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-dru-smith-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=November 25, 2022|access-date=November 25, 2022}} However, on December 11, he signed a second two-way contract.{{cite tweet|author=Miami HEAT|title=OFFICIAL: The Miami HEAT have signed Orlando Robinson to a two-way contract and have waived Dru Smith.|number=1601987170935480320|user=MiamiHEAT|date=December 11, 2022|access-date=December 11, 2022}} The Heat made the [[2023 NBA Finals]], but lost to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in five games. As a player under a two-way contract, Robinson was ineligible to play in the [[2023 NBA playoffs|playoffs]]. On July 1, 2023, the Heat signed Robinson to a two-year standard contract, relieving him of his co-assignment to the Skyforce.{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN ORLANDO ROBINSON|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-orlando-robinson-2|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2023|access-date=July 2, 2023}} On July 7, 2024, the Heat waived Robinson.{{cite web|title=HEAT WAIVE ORLANDO ROBINSON|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waive-orlando-robinson|website=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=July 7, 2024}} ===Sacramento / Stockton Kings (2024–2025)=== On August 7, 2024, Robinson signed a one-year deal with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Orlando Robinson|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-orlando-robinson|website=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2024|access-date=August 7, 2024}} On October 7, 2024, Robinson suffered an [[medial collateral ligament|MCL]] sprain that ruled him out for at least four weeks.{{cite web|title=Kings center Orlando Robinson (knee) out at least four weeks|url=https://sactownsports.com/nba-sacramento-kings-orlando-robinson-injury-update/|website=SacsTownSports.com|access-date=October 21, 2024}} Throughout the season, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Stockton Kings]].{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Stockton Kings Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Stockton-Kings/56/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 29, 2024}} On January 7, 2025, he was waived by the Kings.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Kings Waive Orlando Robinson|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/01/kings-to-waive-orlando-robinson.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=January 7, 2025|access-date=January 7, 2025}} ===Toronto Raptors (2025)=== On January 18, 2025, Robinson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]]{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN ROBINSON TO 10-DAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-robinson-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 18, 2025|access-date=January 18, 2025}} and ten days later, he signed a second one.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN ROBINSON TO SECOND 10-DAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-robinson-to-second-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2025|access-date=January 28, 2025}} Following the expiration of his second 10-day contract, Robinson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Raptors on February 7.{{cite web|title= RAPTORS CONVERT BATTLE AND SIGN ROBINSON|url= https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-convert-battle-and-sign-robinson|website=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2025}} In 35 appearances (8 starts) for Toronto, he averaged 8.1 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 1.9 assists. On April 10, Robinson was waived by the Raptors.{{Cite web|title=Raptors waive forward Cole Swider and centre Orlando Robinson|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/raptors-waive-forward-cole-swider-and-centre-orlando-robinson/|access-date=April 10, 2025|website=sportsnet.ca|language=en}} === Orlando Magic (2025–2026) === On July 21, 2025, Robinson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web | title=Orlando Magic Sign Orlando Robinson to Two-Way Contract | website=NBA | date=2025-07-21 | url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-orlando-robinson-to-two-way-contract-20250718 | access-date=2025-12-06}} He made four appearances (including one start) for Orlando, averaging 1.8 points, 1.0 rebound, and 0.8 assists. On February 17, 2026, Robinson was waived by the Magic following the signing of [[Alex Morales]].{{Cite web|title=Magic Sign Free Agent Alex Morales to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-free-agent-alex-morales-to-two-way-contract-20260217|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=nba.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA
